In [[abstract algebra|algebra]], the '''Gorenstein–Walter theorem''', proved by [[Daniel Gorenstein|Gorenstein]] and [[John H. Walter|Walter]],{{sfnp|Gorenstein|Walter|1965a}}{{sfnp|Gorenstein|Walter|1965b}}{{sfnp|Gorenstein|Walter|1965c}} states that if a [[finite group]] ''G'' has a [[dihedral group|dihedral]] [[Sylow 2-subgroup]], and ''O''(''G'') is the maximal [[normal subgroup]] of odd [[order (group theory)|order]], then ''G''/''O''(''G'') is isomorphic to a [[p-group|2-group]], or the [[alternating group]] ''A''<sub>7</sub>, or a subgroup of PΓL<sub>2</sub>(''q'') containing PSL<sub>2</sub>(''q'') for ''q'' an odd prime power. Note that A<sub>5</sub> ≈ PSL<sub>2</sub>(4) ≈ PSL<sub>2</sub>(5) and A<sub>6</sub> ≈ PSL<sub>2</sub>(9).
